reason: Start with the wide companions to address what can separate two stars.
expectation: The passing star may gravitationally pull the wide pair apart without damaging either star.

alternatives.reason: The close pair is also relevant, but the wide pair seems more vulnerable to separation.

effect: The wide pair separated without a collision, completing the first goal; I’ll follow the closer encounters next.
reaction: The distinction between surviving stars and a broken pair was satisfying.
reason: The close pair directly addresses the remaining goal.
expectation: The passing star may alter the close pair’s orbit, though I’m unsure whether it will separate them.

alternatives.reason: The unequal pair is another close-companion encounter, but I’ll start with the close pair.

reaction: The passing star’s escape was surprising.
reason: The unequal pair is the only remaining combination and continues the closer-companion goal.

effect: The heavier newcomer replaced the lighter companion, completing the closer-encounters goal and the chapter.
reaction: The exchange was a clear, satisfying contrast with the earlier ejection.

mostWorthwhile.text: The close-pair encounter was most worthwhile: tightening the pair while ejecting the passing star made the gravitational interaction interesting.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final encounter was less engaging as a decision because it was the only combination left, though its outcome was clear.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the close pair became more tightly bound while the passing star escaped the cluster.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless; each encounter addressed a stated goal, although the compatible menu supplied the possible actions.

continue.text: Yes. The contrasting outcomes of the stellar encounters made me curious about where the departing stars go.
